matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: First compute the integer values of both sides of the equation and determine the numeric imbalance. Then look for a single‑stick move whose numeric effect (e.g., ±1, ±5, ±6) matches the imbalance (or its opposite). This guides the choice of which numeral or operator to modify.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is false and you need to decide which stick to move to restore equality.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick arbitrarily without checking the numeric difference, ending up with the same imbalance.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and a V appears, you can increase its value by 5 by repositioning one of its diagonal sticks to create an X (two crossing diagonals). The extra diagonal must come from another symbol that can spare it without becoming invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to raise a numeral by 5 and a V is present, and you have a spare diagonal stick.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from V and discarding it, leaving V invalid.

matchstick.title: Change + to - and add I
matchstick.principle: To turn a plus sign into a minus sign, remove its vertical stick; then place that stick as a solitary I on a numeral, increasing that numeral by 1. This simultaneously reduces the RHS by 6 (changing + to –) and raises the chosen numeral by 1, adjusting the total by +7.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a plus sign is present and you need to decrease the RHS by 6 while also increasing a numeral by 1.
matchstick.example: Changing + to – but forgetting to add the vertical stick to a numeral, leaving the equation with a missing I.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: If a numeral contains more than one I (i.e., multiple vertical sticks), you can move one of those I sticks to another numeral, decreasing the source by 1 and increasing the target by 1. Ensure both source and target remain valid Roman numerals after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need a ±1 adjustment and a numeral with extra I's is available.
matchstick.example: Moving an I from a solitary I, which eliminates that numeral entirely.

matchstick.title: Change - to = by adding a horizontal stick from a numeral
matchstick.principle: To convert a minus sign into an equals sign, you need a second horizontal stick. Take that stick from a numeral that can lose a horizontal segment (e.g., an X or a V that can become I) without becoming invalid, and attach it to the minus sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you have a minus sign that should become = and a numeral with a removable horizontal stick.
matchstick.example: Taking a horizontal stick from a numeral that cannot lose it, making the numeral invalid.

matchstick.title: When converting - to +, also move a vertical stick to form a valid plus sign
matchstick.principle: Changing a minus sign to a plus sign requires adding a vertical stick. Obtain that vertical stick from a numeral that can spare an I (i.e., a numeral with at least two I's) without becoming invalid, and attach it to the minus sign to form +.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to turn – into + and have an extra vertical stick available.
matchstick.example: Turning – into + without supplying a vertical stick, leaving an incomplete plus sign.

matchstick.title: Swap '-' and '=' by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: If both a minus sign and an equals sign appear, you can exchange them by moving one horizontal stick from the = to the –. This turns the – into = (by gaining a second horizontal) and the = into – (by losing one horizontal). Ensure the resulting = still has two horizontals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to replace a minus with an equals (or vice versa) and both operators are present.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal from = to – but leaving = with only one horizontal, breaking the equality sign.

matchstick.title: Ensure a valid '=' remains when moving a stick from '='
matchstick.principle: If you relocate any stick from the equality sign, you must keep two horizontal sticks to preserve a valid =. Any move that leaves only one horizontal stick results in an invalid operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering taking a stick from the = sign.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal from = and leaving only one line, which is no longer an equals sign.

matchstick.title: Convert X to V to subtract 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and an X appears, you can decrease its value by 5 by removing one of its diagonal sticks, turning the X into a V. The removed stick must be placed elsewhere to keep the total stick count unchanged.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to lower a numeral by 5 and an X is present.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from X and discarding it, leaving X invalid.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from a numeral that cannot lose a stick without becoming invalid (e.g., X, V, solitary I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the numeric effect of the move without checking whether the source numeral can still represent a valid Roman numeral after losing that stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Before moving a stick, verify that the source numeral can lose that stick and still be a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.description: Providing an incomplete equation after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model forgets to reconstruct the full equation after the transformation, omitting a character or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always rewrite the entire equation after the move, ensuring all symbols are present and correctly spaced.

matchstick.description: Changing – to + without adding the required vertical stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes the operator shape changes automatically and neglects the need for an extra vertical segment.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When turning – into +, also move a vertical stick from a numeral that can spare it, so the plus sign is complete.

matchstick.description: Using an angled stick as a vertical stick (or vice versa)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model ignores the orientation constraint of matchsticks, treating diagonal sticks as interchangeable with vertical ones.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Respect stick orientation: only vertical sticks can form I, only diagonal sticks can form V or X.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from the equality sign and leaving no valid '=' sign in the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model overlooks the requirement that = must consist of two horizontal sticks.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never remove a stick from = unless you simultaneously add another horizontal to keep it as a valid =.
